finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.untrusted_source: cin >> n; cin >> m; cin >> k; cin >> h;
finding.trigger: User input is directly used in calculations without any validation or sanitization.
finding.assumptions: The code does not involve any command execution or shell interpretation. The variables `n`, `m`, `k`, and `h` are used in calculations and do not influence any command execution.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: User input is directly stored in the vector `v` without any bounds checking.
finding.assumptions: The vector `v` is properly initialized with size `n` and the loop iterates `n` times. However, if `n` is not properly validated or controlled, it could lead to a buffer overflow.

finding.title: Integer Overflow
finding.trigger: User input could lead to integer overflow when performing division or modulo operations.
finding.assumptions: The values of `v[i]` and `k` are not validated to ensure they do not cause overflow. If `k` is zero, it will cause a division by zero error.

finding.assumptions: The code does not involve any command execution or shell interpretation. The variable `ans` is used in output and does not influence any command execution.
